issues.legal_issue: Roads and drains that are functional adjuncts to a factory may qualify as buildings for depreciation purposes.
material_facts: The assessee companies claimed depreciation on the costs or written-down values of roads within factory premises, including roads linking factory buildings or providing access to them.
The roads were used to support factory business activities, including movement of materials, products and workers.
In connected matters, depreciation was also claimed on drains within factory premises, which formed part of the factory’s infrastructure.
issues.conclusion: Roads within factory premises that link or provide access to factory buildings and are necessary adjuncts to business activity, and drains integral to the convenient use of the factory, are buildings for depreciation purposes; the expenditure or written-down value attributable to them is eligible for depreciation.
issues.legal_principle: Section 32 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 allows depreciation on business capital assets, calculated on written-down value, to determine net taxable income. A depreciation or relief provision is construed reasonably and in favour of the assessee, using a purposive and contextual interpretation; the ordinary meaning of building is not confined to a structure with walls and a roof. The Court relied on C.I.T. v. Ram Gopal Mills Ltd. on depreciation and written-down value; C.I.T. v. Alps Theatre on the purpose of allowances; C.I.T. v. Taj Mahal Hotel on purposive interpretation of plant; Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay v. Indian Oil Corporation Ltd. on buildings; and the consistent High Court approach in C.I.T. v. Colour Chem Ltd., C.I.T. v. Lucas-TVS Ltd., Panyem Cement and Chemical Industries Ltd. v. Addl. C.I.T., C.I.T. v. Kalyani Spinning Mills Ltd., C.I.T. v. Mec. Gaw Laboratories India Ltd. and C.I.T. v. Bangalore Turf Club Ltd. The Court also referred to Raja Jagadambika Pratap Narain Singh v. C.B.D.T. and Azam Jah Bahadur v. E.T.O. on interpreting taxing statutes, and explained C.I.T. v. Alps Theatre as not determining the treatment of roads.

rule.if: depreciation_claim_proceeding and ((factory_roads_link_buildings and roads_support_business_activity) or (factory_drains_integral_to_factory and drains_enable_convenient_factory_use))

predicates.depreciation_claim_proceeding: An assessee sought depreciation on capital expenditure or written-down value relating to property used in a business.
predicates.factory_roads_link_buildings: The assessee laid roads within factory premises that link factory buildings or provide access to them.
predicates.roads_support_business_activity: The factory roads are used to support the assessee’s business activity.
predicates.factory_drains_integral_to_factory: The assessee constructed drains that form an integral part of the factory.
predicates.drains_enable_convenient_factory_use: The drains contribute to the convenient use of the factory.

issues.definition: When a depreciation claim concerns factory roads that link buildings and support business activity, or drains integral to and enabling convenient factory use, those roads or drains are treated as buildings entitled to depreciation.

issues.legal_issue: The later inclusion of roads in depreciation rules does not imply that roads were excluded from the meaning of buildings for earlier periods.
material_facts: The revenue argued that rules which later expressly included roads as buildings applied only prospectively and therefore roads could not qualify as buildings for earlier periods.
The rule-making authority included roads and other structures in the building category while prescribing fixed depreciation rates.
Courts had consistently interpreted the term building to include factory roads, and the department had accepted and acted on that interpretation.
issues.conclusion: The later rules’ prospective operation does not establish that roads were excluded from buildings in earlier periods; the amendment prescribed rates and did not displace the earlier interpretation that qualifying roads formed part of a building.
issues.legal_principle: Validly made rules have the same force as provisions of the Act, but the later inclusion of roads and prescription of fixed rates enlarged or clarified the treatment of buildings and did not whittle down the earlier scope of section 32. A statute is ordinarily prospective unless expressly or by necessary implication made otherwise. An interpretation consistently given over time and accepted and acted upon by the department should not normally be upset without circumstances warranting a fresh look. The Court relied on C.I.T. v. Bangalore Turf Club Ltd. and Saharanpur Electric Supply Co. Ltd. v. C.I.T.

rule.if: depreciation_claim_proceeding and pre_amendment_period_claimed and later_rules_expressly_include_roads and consistent_prior_interpretation_included_roads

predicates.depreciation_claim_proceeding: An assessee sought depreciation on property used in a business.
predicates.pre_amendment_period_claimed: The depreciation claim concerns a period before later rules took effect.
predicates.later_rules_expressly_include_roads: Later rules expressly include roads within the category used to determine depreciation treatment.
predicates.consistent_prior_interpretation_included: Courts had consistently interpreted the relevant category to include roads, and the department had accepted and acted on that interpretation.

issues.definition: If a depreciation claim concerns an earlier period, later rules expressly include roads, and a consistent prior interpretation included roads, the later rules do not exclude qualifying roads from the earlier building treatment.
